label: Extended Confucian moral self-cultivation to women's classical education
description: Writing in the Eastern Han dynasty, Ban Zhao drew upon Confucian ethics of harmony, ritual propriety (li), and self-cultivation to argue explicitly that daughters must be educated alongside sons.
dialecticalTension: Applies universal Confucian learning within patriarchal Han household norms to secure female literacy.
historicalContext: Composed in Lessons for Women (Nüjie, c. 106 CE) at the imperial Han court.

citations.author: Nancy Lee Swann
citations.work: Pan Chao: Foremost Woman Scholar of China

label: Informed Confucian virtue psychology and moral education
description: Ban Zhao shared Mencius's conviction that moral virtue requires deliberate scholarly cultivation and ritual reflection across human relationships.
dialecticalTension: Extends Mencian moral pedagogy to female scholars and household educators.

citations.author: Robin R. Wang
citations.work: Images of Women in Chinese Thought and Culture

label: Applied Ren and Li to reciprocal spousal respect and female education
description: In Nüjie, Ban Zhao argued that harmony (he) and ritual propriety (li) break down if women are denied the classical texts required to cultivate moral judgment.
dialecticalTension: Reveals an internal tension within Confucian ritualism between hierarchy and universal moral education.
